nodes.text: Hallgrim and the other Kolskegg. I know them to be the greatest
fighting men, and this besides, that they have such good weapons.
Hallgrim has a halberd which he has had enchanted
to this end, that no weapon shall be his death but it. This
goes with it too: it is known at once when a killing is to be done with the halberd,
for then it sings loudly beforehand. So great a property
it has. Kolskegg has a short sword. That is the
best of weapons. They have a force a third larger than yours.
They also have much wealth and have hidden it on land, and I know
forefathers in the male line, been christened. After that they went from Skogahverfi
to Hofdabrekka. By then everything was known ahead about
their journey. There was a man called Galdra-Hedin who lived in Kerlingardal. There
the heathen men struck a bargain with him that he should kill
Thangbrand and his company. And he went up onto Arnarstakksheid
and held a great sacrifice there. When Thangbrand rode from the east,
the earth burst apart under Thangbrand's horse, but
he leapt off the horse and got up onto the bank, and the earth
swallowed the horse with all its gear, and they never saw it
again. Then Thangbrand praised God.
The Killing of Galdra-Hedin
Gudleif searches for Galdra-Hedin and finds him on the heath
nor edge, and the heathen men were very afraid. Then Thangbrand asked
whether people would accept the faith, but all the heathen men spoke
strongly against it. I will give you a choice, says Thangbrand, so that you can
test which faith is better. We shall make fires,
three of them. And you heathen men shall consecrate one, and I another,
and the third shall be unconsecrated. And if the berserk fears
the one I consecrated but wades through yours, then you shall
accept the faith. That is well spoken, says Gest, and to this I will
agree for myself and my household. And when Gest had
said this, many more agreed, and there was at that
a great cheer. Then it is told that the berserk was coming to the farm,
and the fires were then made and burning. People then took their weapons
and jumped up onto the benches and waited so. The berserk
runs up with weapons and in at the door. He comes into the hall,
further in, and at once wades through the fire that the heathens
had consecrated, and he comes to the fire that Thangbrand had consecrated,
and dared not wade that fire, and said he was burning all over. He
strikes with his sword up at the bench, [and it] caught in the crossbeam as he
swung high. Thangbrand struck the arm with a crucifix,
and so great a miracle happened that the sword fell from the hand
of the berserk. Then Thangbrand thrusts a sword into his chest,
and Gudleif struck at the arm so that it came off. Then there went at [him]
would give my property that this had not come
about. Bad seed has been sown, and evil will
grow from it. From there he rode over Arnarstakksheid and to Solheimar
in the evening. Lodmund Ulfsson lived there, and
he was a great friend of Flosi's, and he stayed there the night. And in the morning
